title: Normalized reduction identification data
statement: Let A,B be categories with shifts by the integers on B, and L:A→B and R:B→A functors. Fix X₁,X₃,Z in A, H,Q in B, c:RQ→Z, η₁:X₁→RLX₁, η₃:X₃→RLX₃, p:X₃→Z and κ:X₁→R(H[1]). A normalized reduction identification is a record of isomorphisms αF:LX₃≅Q and αB:LX₁≅H[1], together with the equations η₃ followed by R(αF) and c equals p and η₁ followed by R(αB) equals κ. Specialization to the derived scalar adjunction unit and the quotient and Kummer maps is exactly the normalized identification data in the divisible extension reduction statement.

source.place: Paragraphs 4 and 5, normalized quotient and Kummer identifications; abstract record of the same data, not a verbatim source definition.

proof_origin.place: The four fields of the existing Identifications record, abstracted over categories, functors and normalization maps.

from.place: The normalized identification data in the divisible reduction statement.

proof.text: Use the record with precisely four fields alphaF, alphaB, quotient_unit and kummer_unit. Its specialization has exactly the previous Identifications field types: insert the derived scalar unit for η₁ and η₃, the canonical single/restriction isomorphism for c, the single quotient map for p and the canonical restricted Kummer boundary for κ. No existence or arbitrary object choice is used in the definition.
